editorial:
Ever feel like you are just not ready to grow up? That is exactly where you find Matt, a smart MIT grad who decides to ditch the corporate world to work at a video store. He is basically hiding from adulthood until his old high school crush, Tori, pops into the shop. She invites him to a huge end-of-summer party, and suddenly Matt is desperate to prove he is actually cool and successful. Along with his twin sister and his goofy best friend, he tries to fake a fancy life to impress her. It is a lighthearted ride that captures that awkward feeling of being stuck between being a kid and an adult.

The movie keeps things moving fast with plenty of laughs and relatable moments of social panic. While the plot is pretty predictable, the chemistry between the leads makes it work. You will probably find yourself rooting for Matt even when he is making terrible choices. If you want a relaxing night in, you should try streaming this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture. If you prefer to own your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this feel-good story on your shelf.
endingExplained: After a series of lies and embarrassing mishaps at the party, Matt finally stops pretending to be someone he is not. He admits to Tori that he is just a guy working at a video store. Instead of being turned off, Tori appreciates his honesty and the fact that he is actually grounded. They end up together, and Matt finds a balance between his intelligence and his desire to enjoy life on his own terms.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward romantic comedies and stories about growing up.
